summary: Exelon answers PJM's November 4, 2026 request for more time and opposition to fast-track processing in the EL27-11 complaint. Exelon says PJM's requested extension is too long for the narrow legal question, supports a shorter extension, and asks for an order well before the May 2027 auction.
ask: Limit the extension to December 7, 2026, and issue an order sufficiently in advance of the May 2027 Base Residual Auction.

points.point: Exelon says PJM's proposed extension is excessive for the narrow scope of the allegations it must answer.
points.quote: the scale of PJM’s proposed extension is excessive for the narrow scope of the allegations it must answer.

points.point: Exelon says it should not take PJM 48 days to state its view on the narrow legal question.
points.quote: it should not take PJM 48 days to express its opinion on this narrow legal question.

points.point: Exelon supports extending the comment period to December 7, 2026, which gives PJM 34 days after the complaint.
points.quote: Exelon supports an extension of the comment period until December 7, 2026, which will provide PJM with a total of 34 days after Exelon filed the complaint

points.point: Exelon says the relief it seeks is prospective and can be given only before the auction process moves forward.
points.quote: the relief Exelon seeks is prospective, and it can be meaningfully provided only before the auction process moves forward.

throughLine.text: A procedural answer in Exelon's section 206 complaint on PJM's capacity auction schedule. It does not cite the show cause orders; the link is the shared PJM resource adequacy question.

figures.label: Total days PJM would have under Exelon's proposal
figures.quote: a total of 34 days after Exelon filed the complaint
